tool.title: Publish a folio's or an IG's site from the agent's own checkout — the one agent publish path
tool.description: Build a repository's site in the agent's checkout and push it to the publish branch, as a preview or as the main site, without an Actions runner. Which build is read from the repository: a declared `site.build` recipe (built by `build-instance-site`), else the reusable workflow its own workflow files call — `folio-staging.yml` for a folio, the WHO SMART Base IG's `ghbuild.yml` for a FHIR IG, whose `build` job is planned step by step and run as written. For an IG it then applies the harness chrome over the built output (`sync-docs-harness`, then `rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site --instance <the IG>`): every page gains the rail and the icon row `#fa-navbar-row`, and the IG's own content is left byte for byte. A root publish is REFUSED when the chrome cannot be applied, and a clean root deploy is refused over any root whose `index.html` wears the icon row unless the new output does too, so a chromed root is never replaced by bare IG Publisher pages. Every run prints its plan first, and the plan lists the chrome step; `--plan` stops there, `--dry-run` composes the commit in a temporary worktree and pushes nothing, `--artifact` writes a claude.ai Artifact bundle instead.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: The checkout to publish, with the platform's layers mounted at its root. Default: the working directory.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.description: The branch to publish. Default: the checkout's. The default branch publishes the main site; any other a preview.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: A folio preview's base branch, for its ChangeSet and rendered impact.

inputs.name: main
inputs.description: Publish the main site at the root. Implied on the default branch, refused off it.

inputs.name: plan
inputs.description: Print what would be built and where, every step named, and stop.

inputs.name: dryRun
inputs.description: Build and compose the commit in a temporary publish-branch worktree; push nothing.

inputs.name: artifact
inputs.description: Write a claude.ai Artifact bundle here instead of pushing.

inputs.name: workflowSource
inputs.description: An IG: read the reusable workflow from this local checkout instead of fetching it at the ref its caller names.

inputs.name: publisher
inputs.description: `folio` or `ig`, when the repository's workflows call both (the folio by default).

inputs.name: runUrl
inputs.description: What the commit and render log name as the run. Default: the commit's URL.

outputs.name: url
outputs.description: Where the site is served once GitHub's Pages deploy has run, with the commit pushed (or, with --dry-run, the commit composed and discarded).

render.reason: a reader opens the published site; the scheme is checked before it reaches an href

selection.when: Every agent-run publish of a folio's or an IG's site, preview or main: it is what the current build pipeline uses (the IG repositories' `site-publish.yml` run this same command on a runner).
selection.limits: An IG repository's main site is built from its AST, read from the cache branch fhir-harness's `ig-ast-refresh` keeps current, by the steps its `site.build` recipe declares (`profile: ig-repo-site`): the theme side bar and search, the harness rail and icon row, the served directories and the `folio-build.json` stamp, measured against the live root (https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools/pull/202). A stale AST is refused, never built from Publisher HTML. A root publish is refused when the composed site lacks anything the current root has (`site-parity`), judged on the pages. Without a `site.build` recipe an IG falls back to its own workflow's Publisher steps, which need a Docker daemon and give the rail and icon row only.
selection.cost: An IG: the whole IG Publisher build (tens of minutes), then about two minutes of rail over ~3,600 pages. A folio: its build command. Then one push, and GitHub's own Pages deploy.

remedies.none: The publish is a push to the repository's publish branch; offline, `--plan` and `--dry-run` still say and build what would be published.

$comment.comment:
── An IG repository's own site: two Tools, one pair of skills ─────────

Owner, 2026-10-14: "It is up to a human or an agent whether to use a tool
or not ... Multiple tools can implement the same skill." Both Tools below
publish an IG repository's own Pages site wearing the harness chrome
(`harness-tiles`) as a staging or main publish (`feature-staging`). They
are NOT derived alternatives: their I/O differs (stage-local takes a
checkout and plan/dry-run flags; the workflow takes a repository and a
ref), so `deriveAlternatives` keeps them apart, and each says in its
`selection` when it is the one to reach for.

`stage-local` is the ONE agent publish path (owner, 2026-10-10: "one
consolidated workflow"; bean n3h9), and until now it had no node: the
`feature-staging` skill described it and nothing in the graph ran it.
Owner, 2026-10-14, decision "1": its IG route now applies the chrome.
